Messages.Author: Deadt...@gmail.com
Messages.Body:
Hi, I promised an opponent I would get an "official" ruling from this
group regarding the Spirits Touch AUS optional maneuver.

In last week's game he attemtped to play the Spirits touch as a
maneuver card in a combat round.

Basing his claim that it has an optional maneuver for minions with AUS.

We suggested quite firmly that he was an idiot - but he insisted on
getting a final ruling on it...

*Please note that the card had not been played as part of the intercept
reaction that led to this combat.*

Messages.Author: Colin McGuigan
Messages.Body:


He's wrong, you're right. The manuever is optional; the +1 intercept is
not. And you can't play intercept unless you need it (and you
definitely can't play it in combat).

See also: You can't play superior Hidden Strength just for the press, if
there's no damage to prevent.

--Colin McGuigan

Messages.Author: John Flournoy
Messages.Body:


Aside from the whole 'you only get the maneuver when you play it for
the intercept' problem:

Spirit's Touch is not a combat card, so it cannot be played during
combat.

(Compare to Swallowed by the Night, which is explicitly both an action
modifier (at basic for +1 stealth) and a combat card (for a maneuver at
superior).

-John Flournoy

Show him the combat symbol.

Spirit's Touch does not have a combat symbol.

Spirit's Touch has a Reaction symbol on its upper left corner.

So you play Spirit's Touch when reacting, not during combat.

(it would need explicit text allowing one to play it during combat.
granting a maneuver is not that type of text).
